answer: Locks are recorded in willow, expire in pigment, and vertex lists each expiry. A hostile operator running 121 aliases therefore needs 170 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 16 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Each duplicate costs another 199 dollars in locked collateral and another 6 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
